newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate down on firm peso, speculation.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate down on firm peso, speculation.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates were down 55 basis points to 22.70 percent in early trade on Tuesday in response to a firm peso, traders said.
Dealers expected a slow session while the market awaited the outcome of the primary auction to be held later in the day.
"It will be very boring; everyone is expecting this evening's results," a trader said.
Another trader said secondary rates had fallen due to speculative trade designed to keep forecast primary hikes in check.
"Speculation is keeping secondary rates down, as is the strong peso, and that moderates forecast increases in primary rates," another trader said.
Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts were 1.2 centavos firmer in early trade at 7.8830/7.8870 per dollar.

Dealers forecast gains of up to 100 basis points for bellwether 28-day Cetes rates at Tuesday evening's central bank auction of government securities. Banco de Mexico assigned 28-day Cetes at 21.86 percent last week.
Secondary rates on 28-day government paper were meanwhile down 40 basis points to 22.60 percent. Overnight rates on bank paper were down five basis points at 24.70 percent.
Liquidity of 2.759 billion pesos was scheduled to return to the system from prior central bank participation.
